title: Random-forest target selection supported nine millisecond pulsar discoveries
summary: A random-forest classifier ranked unidentified Fermi-LAT sources, from which the team selected 79 targets for MeerKAT UHF observations. The survey reported nine new millisecond pulsars, all detected in coherent tied-array beams; seven were also confirmed as Fermi-LAT counterparts through gamma-ray pulsations. This entry covers only the nine MSP discoveries. Six slower pulsars were also reported, but five were found in a wider incoherent beam and are not included in the AI-linked result. The authors note earlier optical redback-candidate identification for PSR J1910−5320 and single-pulse reports in the J0657−4657 beam; no claim is made that these were the first observations at all wavelengths.
ai_technology: Random Forest classifier used to rank unidentified Fermi-LAT sources as pulsar-like candidates
